messages:
marina: heads up — seeing steady GPU memory + page-table growth on a long-context benchmark using paged KV. reproduces on mixed H100/MI250X cluster, ~6GB growth per 1k tokens.
josh: can you drop the repro command and a short log snippet?
marina: sure — quick repro we run locally:```bash
./run_infer --model redwood-v1-paged --ctx 65536 --batch 1 --device-mix h100,mi250x --enable-kvcache-paged --trace-pt=1
```log tail:```txt
[trace] pt_entries=10240 evicted=480 alloc_pages=15360 total_pt_mem=23.1MB
[trace] pt_entries=11200 evicted=520 alloc_pages=16400 total_pt_mem=29.4MB
[trace] pt_entries=12200 evicted=540 alloc_pages=17480 total_pt_mem=35.9MB
[warning] kv_cache: page_reuse_count skewed, reuse_window=4096 -> growth
```i'll attach full logs to the issue.
anika: interesting — reuse_window=4096 suggests LRU splay tree may be degenerating into near-linear behavior for this access pattern. we've seen similar when many small, repetitive prompt fragments create hot tails.
josh: could also be a remap/owner bit mismatch when pages migrate across NVLink vs PCI on MI250X. ordering differences can make evict decisions not compact older entries.
marina: i instrumented the PT walker and saw ghost_count incrementing slowly:```txt
[pt-walk] ghost_count=72 -> 91 -> 108 over 10k steps
```that's the part that correlates with alloc_pages rising.
ci-bot: CI test "kvcache-longctx-stress" failed on h100-mi250x mix (run 23). See <ci/build/4832>
josh: ok plan: open an eng-runtime bug with the trace + minimal repro. try forcing strict LRU (no splay rotatations) and run on both architectures to see if growth stops.
anika: i can add a small deterministic stress harness that toggles reuse_window sizes and simulates NVLink vs PCI ordering. will also add assert to catch owner-bit divergence.
marina: thanks — i'll create the issue and drop the logs + perf flame. tagging @eng-runtime for prioritization. :eyes:
pagerbot: created issue ENG-4521: "kv-paged: LRU splay degeneration + owner-bit divergence on mixed GPU runs" and assigned to eng-runtime.
josh: short term mitigation — we can reduce reuse_window to 1024 in production for those clusters to limit growth while root cause is investigated. :+1:
marina: noted, i'll schedule a canary for tomorrow morning.
